A Papa John's franchise owner once sold two pizzas for $41 in cash - or for 10,000 Bitcoin instead.

He almost said no to the Bitcoin. Six months later it was worth $10,000. Today it's worth $1.3 billion.

Kevin Trudeau says he bought Bitcoin that same year, before almost anyone understood what it was.

The pattern behind every fortune he's watched get made: the money was never in the thing everyone could already see. It was in the thing nobody understood yet.

Would you have taken the cash or the coin?

#kevintrudeau #bitcoin #cryptocurrency #wealthmindset #investing #financialfreedom

In 1999, Kevin Trudeau watched the richest man in Australia lose $27 million in one weekend at the baccarat table - and call it a good weekend.

Kerry Packer explained why. It was the last day of the casino's quarter. A publicly traded company was about to report a windfall, so before the numbers came out he bought the stock. On the weekends he won big, he shorted the same stock instead.

Either way, the casino's own earnings covered his losses and doubled his wins.

He wasn't gambling on the cards. He was trading on public information nobody else bothered to read.

What's the obvious information you've never actually used?

#kevintrudeau #wealthmindset #investing #richmindset #moneytips #financialfreedom

Before Amazon was Amazon, a billionaire called Kevin Trudeau and told him to buy stock in an online bookstore nobody understood yet. He did.

Years later, another call: two guys in a garage were starting a computer company called Apple. The CEO of the largest computer company in the world had just said there was no market for computers in the home. Kevin bought it anyway.

Both calls came from the same place: people who could see the shape of something before it had a name.

What are you dismissing right now that someone else is quietly buying?

#kevintrudeau #wealthmindset #investing #richpeoplethink #applestock #financialfreedom

In 1999, Kevin Trudeau was on a friend's yacht in Sydney Harbor when he had an idea worth repeating.

His friend Rene Rifkin was one of the best stock traders in Australia. Kevin's idea: write down exactly what you buy and exactly what you sell, and send it out. Anyone who just copies you makes what you make.

Rifkin charged $1,000 a month for a one-page newsletter. People made huge returns doing nothing but reading it and copying the moves.

The lesson was never about stocks. It's that the fastest way to a result is finding someone already getting it and copying the exact moves, in order.

Who are you already close enough to copy?

#kevintrudeau #wealthmindset #investing #richpeoplethink #successhabits #financialfreedom

Do you light your home with whale oil anymore? Kevin Trudeau asks it because someone, once, assumed the answer would always be yes.

John D. Rockefeller got rich replacing whale oil with kerosene. Then Thomas Edison and Tesla, backed by JP Morgan, said they could replace kerosene with electricity - and everyone laughed. Wires across the country, into every house? Insane.

The telephone got the same laugh. Wires into every home, coast to coast? Insane.

Every one of those insane ideas made the people who got in early a fortune.

Which insane idea are you laughing at today?
